notes.title: Free prologue with new boss and secret mission!
notes.content:
Greetings!

We are excited to present the new and mysterious free game [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2960560/Union_of_Gnomes_Prologue/]Union of Gnomes: Prologue[/url]. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2960560/Union_of_Gnomes_Prologue/

It combines the creepy atmosphere of dark fantasy, cheerful humor, and, of course, the daring gnomes desperately fighting for their freedom and independence. 
 
[previewyoutube=atZ26XQlAEQ;full][/previewyoutube]

Lead a motley crew of guerrillas to free your captured comrades and escape the tyranny of the ruthless Snow White. For the tenacious players, we've hidden a secret quest within the prologue—conquering it will bring you closer to solving the mystery of the eighth gnome! Look for the clue in the video!

Here's what you'll find in the game:
[list]
[*] One new, unique and terribly dangerous mission!
[*] A dangerous new boss!
[*] A secret quest!
[*] A lot of well-known – and not so well-known – fairy tale characters who fight on the side of evil, trying to suppress and destroy the gnomes!
[*] Create unusual combos with your gnome cards to reach the end of the prologue or die with honor!
[/list]
Once you've finished the prologue (and added [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/2097030/Union_of_Gnomes/]Union of Gnomes[/url] to your Steam Wishlist), you can look forward to the full story of the gnomes' heroic adventures as they fight for their freedom in the full game. The gnomes stand for freedom and the right not to impose subjugation on anyone else!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/2097030/Union_of_Gnomes/ 

Don't forget to recommend the game to your friends and favorite streamers, share your impressions, and leave a review. 

Freedom to Gnomes!
Union of Gnomes Team

notes.title: Tempest: the Quest. Get ready for Halloween! Part 3
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11019625/facf2fd19d900f4704b0ed1b28dee3b514288ae1.png[/img]
Ahoy, captain! We continue our Halloween themed [url=https://steamcommunity.com/linkfilter/?url=https://steamcommunity.com/ogg/418180/announcements/detail/1582378649880479023]quest[/url] and this is your last chance to join since next Monday will reveal the terrifying end of this story. The comments to the previous installment reveal a pretty even split between the options and a wonderful spinoff on the life of second mate [b]Fuhrer_51[RUS][/b]. Seems pretty intriguing so far!

___

You can't help but feel that sound nagging you, distracting you, filling your mind with trouble and disquiet. You must examine it.

You cross paths with the second mate as you go down into the holds, and he nods as he clearly heads to the rescued man. Fair enough, to each man his own, and you won't be standing in his way while he's doing his job, whatever it is.

The holds are dark: you take a dim light from the hook by the entrance and give it some fuel. Shaky light fills room after room filled to the roof with containers well-bound to the floor and walls. As shadows dance on the walls with your every move, you realize the sound has shifted: the whistling is coming from all around you now. With the deep sea behind every wall, no matter where you look, your predicament seems impossible.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11019625/0adc67f3e7a97f8b097ba88f06280e67a918fd59.png[/img]
Slowly, you continue moving between the crates as a deep, aching pain begins to pierce your temples. Then suddenly, a patch of light catches an odd inscription, seemingly carved into the boards ages ago: *849JB*

You trace the writing with your fingers, and the whistling dies down for an instant, but you are certain: those symbols now belong to you, forever. Your hands begin to tremble at this unexpected realization.

You raise the lantern higher, and spot similar inscriptions everywhere the light falls. *B8Y90* above your head, and a bit to the left “B8BMX*. Panic rises in the back of your throat, and you scramble to reach the other end of the holds as more and more inscriptions appear in the dancing light, so meaningless at first. The whistling is almost gone, replaced by a new woe: persistent memories of strange sigils that had never been here before. You're certain, you were the one to affix this cargo here and remember inspecting the entire hold.

Then you tumble as something rams into your legs. That you manage to catch the lantern seems almost a miracle now. You lie still on the boards for some seconds, staring at yet another missive just over your face *R5G05* Time passes: you don't know how much. *8F5F3*, keeps spinning in your head; *KA9D5*, it echoes and reverberates.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11019625/4a6eac2338274589e841124bd0c8da8ed84d241c.png[/img]
You realize you have to get up, and you manage to recall the captain's orders, but before you can do anything, the vessel shakes once, then more and more, and then it goes quiet. You already know what it means, so you run. Through the holds, up the stairs, then higher and higher, not even letting your eyes adjust to the light. You throw the doors open, fully ready to face the blinding light, but instead, you face the tumult right as it reaches its peak.

Whatever you expected to see, you did not expect this.

You see sailors running to and fro; you hear bits of orders, screams of panic; you feel someone shoulder-checking you, but the man disappears before your eyes can see him; all enveloped, enshrouded in fog dotted with shining orange sparks coming from elsewhere, brought forth by lights you cannot see; and it's like the world is burning, but the air is as cold as before. Perhaps, even colder still.

The captain sees you and heads toward you from the foredeck.

“Did you speak to the man?” he asks you, his face so familiar and yet strange, lit by unnatural, otherworldly light.

*CNWDP*, you say slowly.

“He's ready to talk,” comes the second mate's reply from behind your shoulder. “At least now he seems able to talk.”

Captain's eyes remain transfixed to you. “What did you just say?”

“QKQBV*, you say, unsure what your superior finds so perplexing, *G57F3*

As you turn to face the second made, a question leaves your lips: “Have you seen the writing down in the holds?”

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11019625/6e0e3671b8d1c360f8ff25ba119638ca61d56694.png[/img]
He shakes his head in return: now there are two grown men looking you over for signs of madness. Several long seconds pass before you hear new words: “We just ran aground, and there ain't supposed to be anything to run aground on here. Both of you, get in the water and scout the area. But first, I want you to come to your senses. I'll talk with the gentleman in the meantime. Fuhrer_51[RUS], ready the boat and choose several men for the crew.”

The captain then turns around and heads to hatch belowdecks.
The second mate continues to stare at you: “Can you perform your duty?”

You just stand there, surrounded by the noise and motion and the milky-red glow and the building pressure, both outside and inside your head, as something calls to you; begs to be let out, out into your confused thoughts, but you should be able to get a hold of yourself if need be.

1. We have to figure out what's going on. I am ready to set onto the water immediately.
2. I'm not sure I can muster enough concentration to avoid hindering the team like this.

notes.title: Tempest: the Quest. Get ready for Halloween! Part 2
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11019625/0624c623bf8506aa91de6e3670873834e0958bb8.png[/img]
Hey, pirates! Recently, we have started a Halloween themed [url=https://steamcommunity.com/ogg/418180/announcements/detail/1582378649880479023]quest[/url] and you did a great job participating in it. Now it's time to face the consequences of your actions. If you've missed the start — don't worry, you can join now!

___

You slowly approach the crowd of sailors around the rescued man as a sense of foreboding sets in. There's no way to press through to the captain. You spot a familiar face nearby, an old friend made over many a shift together on watch.

"There's a wrecked ship somewhere overboard, all around us in pieces. We're right next to where she ended."

The news start spreading from man to man, getting louder and louder, and soon enough it reaches the command.

Second mate Fuhrer_51[RUS], leaning over the man, says it first:
"Was there an engagement?"
The poor soul's eyes are speechless and full of terror. With nothing on hand but his own good judgment, the sailor decides to make up his mind.
"A ship musta been wrecked nearby. Prolly more than one," he says, turning to address the captain. "Not to sound like a coward, cap'n, but our ship, she ain't prepared for a fight like this."
Fortune favors the brave, but better to be wary than dead. All the more so with the ship loaded to the brim. And as always, taking a bad risk is bound to cost you your load, your ship, and even your life.
"Ho! Helmsman!" the captain yells. "Swing 'er round!"

A sense of release cuts through the tension. As all hands get ready, the men take the rescued soul away for some food and warmth. You overhear the captain grumbling as you follow the guest out with your eyes:
"Can't be taking no risks right now, afraid."

Slowly the ship starts to crawl through the thick, billowing fog, without a sound save for the splashing waves and creaking rigging. The quiet chatter of the crew drowns in the thick air. With visibility measuring in a few feet, even the slowest possible pace makes for a treacherous traverse.

You glance at the captain, a tall, mighty mast of a man who has spent his entire life at sea, and wait for him to order the sails taken in until the fog clears. But then you see him anxiously fidgeting with one of the keys scattered across the deck. His eyes dim and brow furrowed, it's clear that the man has been hollowed by anxiety far deeper than any sailor so well experienced ought ever feel.

Then, suddenly, there's a loud strike against the broadside.  Unthinkably, the captain, a man of unparalleled mettle, startles before your eyes and rushes toward the sound, struggling to temper his own haste.

The crew, utterly astonished, are confronted by an enormous tree, roots and all, floating placidly atop the waves. It could not, should not be here. Even a cabin boy fresh into his second season on this route would know well enough: a full day's sail separates this point from the nearest island.

"What the devil?" sputters a surprised voice on your left.
"Maybe it was a storm?" another follows hesitantly.

"There was no storm," comes the captain's grim reply. It occurs to you that he began to understand a thing or two about your bizarre predicament. His eyes, broody and dim just a moment ago, are slowly starting to clear, but the utter despair forming on his face instead stuns you. 

"Keep up the pace!" comes his voice, loud and booming, a tone as empty and distant as the woe in his eyes.

"Too dangerous, cap'n," says the chief mate, watching the waves. "There's like to be, aha, yet more debris and trouble oer’board."

"Indeed there is." The mast of a man suddenly shrugs, focusing his gaze on you, and follows it up suddenly with a dejected smile. "This shan't be your last traverse. Go pay that barmy a visit, see if he's talking any sense now."

The captain is captain, and orders are orders. And yet, as your feet lead you into the holds, his strange words and actions keep spinning in your head. And as you keep pondering, the atmosphere of quiet danger grows more and more uneasy. It takes you a while to come back from your thoughts to the quiet, long, whistling sound, not unlike the sound strong winds make as they blow through a crack in the boards. You don't just hear it, you FEEL it, and it's coming from the lower holds, where the goods are kept.

1. Follow the captain's orders and go see the rescued man
2. Climb down for a brief moment to see where that sound is coming from.

notes.title: Tempest: the Quest. Get ready for Halloween!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11019625/4744a2eab98a28543d4bf50fe5fe533ce4cfdcac.jpg[/img]
Ahoy, Pirates! There are some treacherous waters ahead, so you'd better look out for squalls! After all, we all know that October is the time when evil spirits set about their dark deeds. At the very end of the month here on Steam, we will be hosting a big giveaway, but first, you're in for a terrifying journey to uncharted islands.

All you need to do to take part is to keep up with the game news. Every other day, we will release an installment of a story that we will be writing together with you, with a choice for everyone to make at the end of each chapter. Every vote in the comments will be taken into account, and for those that want to flesh out their answers, the story might play out in a very different way.

You'll encounter some pleasant surprises along the way, so we encourage you to keep up with our updates. ;)

And now, let's get started.

_____

You are part of a crew of seasoned sailors that have braved the seas many times together. Each one of you dreams of captaining a ship one day, free to sail the seas under their own flag. But for now, all of you pitch in and pull your weight for a common cause.

It's been four days since you left a trading port. Your ship is set on a well-traveled and familiar course through calm waters, the wind is favorable and fast, and the clouds on the horizon threaten a cold fall shower that might dispel the thickening mist, which has been gently creeping aboard since midday.

A deck boy climbs up the rigging towards the crow's nest, peering intently into the distance once he settles there. Any sailor, no matter how experienced, knows how dangerous sea fogs are, how quickly they can lead a ship off course and run it aground over underwater rocks. The captain has good cause for concern: the ship is sitting exceptionally low, its holds chock-full of goods to sell.

The first mate gives a call to trim the sails and slow down. As the ship decelerates, a milky-white shroud creeps over the deck and keeps rising, faster than anyone expected. Your bewildered crewmates carry on, looking around uneasily now and then, and somewhere in the shadows, you hear a quiet murmur. "The boatswain has always been rather religious," you think to yourself.

"Man overboard!" Suddenly, a muffled and unnaturally distant cry rings out over the deck from the nest. Sailors rush to the side to see a shoddily cobbled-together boat swaying on the waves nearby, and a man clinging to it. His body is submerged, only his head and one hand still above water to clutch at the frail wooden frame.

"Pull him up," the captain orders.

You go about rescuing the man quickly. He's completely exhausted after staying in the water for so long, his muscles cramped, his body ice-cold and almost lifeless.
As soon as you haul the poor fellow aboard, he starts coughing up a lung. 

"Don't go there," he croaks. "Turn back. Turn back."

The sailors huddle around, clearly confused.

"There are keys," one of the men who dragged the poor fellow out of the water pipes up. "Lotsa keys in the boat."
With these words, he opens his hand, and several thuds onto the boards. Silver and gold, in all shapes and sizes. They look mesmerizing, alluring, and somehow filled with promise.

AG7QE-0650A-28DLP
P794W-YWWIC-B6ZPM
R4YX3-L5WXE-ZG89I

The captain kneels near the saved man and asks where he hails from. "What sinking ship did you flee?" The saved man answers with a hoarse, "No, don't go, they're all there."

The man, his grim words, and the frigid, unnatural fog all fill you with dread. You step aside and look at the madman's boat tied to a boom. As your eyes glide over the water, you notice something dark floating on the surface. Straining to focus, you manage to make out some planks. They look like pieces of wreckage, but you're absolutely sure that just a little while ago before the thick fog settled in, there was no sign of another ship anywhere nearby.

Irrational fear grips you. It seems the whole crew has gathered around the saved man and hasn't noticed your predicament. You consider your options:

Tell the captain a wrecked ship might be nearby.
Keep silent.

___

Leave a comment with the number of your reply down below. If you feel like it, you can give a more detailed answer alongside the number. ;)
You have 12 hours to think this through.

[h1]What does it take to be a governor?[/h1]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11019625/d8fd8797e517b371cc62502a23b6f1b64b25d2b7.jpg[/img]
Generally, your city will have 3 stages of development, and as a promising governor, you get to control a simple settlement first (stage 0). This will net you a warehouse where you can store all of the goods that your beloved ship couldn’t contain. To progress to the next stage, you will have to make a certain financial investment and complete a few quests. 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11019625/a529b46631c1c37f7e8271cf51b1d4a703ae04b1.jpg[/img]
Get ready to provide your new home with proper protection, do favors for fellow traders (generous rewards included), search for missing people that got themselves in serious trouble, fight hideous sea monsters and punish thieves among your crew. Sounds like some great adventures are waiting for you, captain!

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11019625/ff4b545421f4c8cbca12520efd38861d23a7ee27.jpg[/img]
With each new stage, your city will get bigger: new taverns and shops will unlock, giving you access to more experienced crew members for hire, as well as valuable goods that you can acquire. Eventually, your fame as a city leader will expand so much that some sailors would be honored to work on your vessel absolutely for free!       

[b]PS.[/b] next week will bring more information about another exciting feature coming to the Pirate City DLC [img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11019625/d6a6dfd4275d45519cc6f099fbbb48daa51024b0.png[/img]

notes.title: Announcing the Pirate City DLC + new update
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11019625/d1b5d432e26ae2062013649ec7fe08d9aefb22ae.jpg[/img]
Ahoy, fellow pirates! We’ve got some great news for everyone who already roves the seas of Tempest or was looking for a perfect opportunity to join our crew. A long-awaited expansion, the [b]Pirate City DLC[/b], is going to be released soon on Steam along with the basic game getting an update. So, what shiny new treasures should you expect? 

[h1]New mechanics are coming[/h1]

First of all, Pirate City adds one of the highly requested features: an ability to build and develop your own settlement. By being a thoughtful governor you will be able to turn a simple village into a thriving city... and get quite a few new quests!  https://youtu.be/eUHPIJHkvGE Other than that, you will be able to buy a share in any shop no matter where it is located. This will certainly improve your financial situation so you can invest even more funds in your own city and make your neighbors envious of your success!

Players can also expect a brand new sinister looking ship that goes under the name of [i]Grim Reaper[/i] and can be decorated with [b]4[/b] extra figureheads: wolf, tiger, bear and lion. Here’s a teaser of the brig in action, which is available for boarding and capturing (but only the bravest may dare —  the crew of this ship is a bit... unusual):

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11019625/d096e3dbf51b9267d47866d9501b73dd5aaa228b.jpg[/img]

We are also introducing a land based battle arena that will be located near your city, so you can test your captain’s melee fighting skills against skeletons and pirate zombies. Yes, we said PIRATE ZOMBIES =) 

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11019625/1e0d756b02c29f7b032880672714e618f9a6bd2e.jpg[/img]

Enter the arena, pick a weapon of choice and get ready to rumble! The more waves of enemies you can survive, the bigger the reward! New achievements included ;)

[h1]The Base game (Tempest) gets an update[/h1]

Along with the release of the Pirate City DLC, the base game will also feature a general overhaul including an updated tutorial, improved water physics and some updates to visuals. Plus, quite a few bugs were sent to walk the plank!

More details to follow regarding our next DLC and the patch in future updates, so stay in touch, captains! [img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/11019625/d6a6dfd4275d45519cc6f099fbbb48daa51024b0.png[/img]

Ahoy, landlubbers! The first DLC for open-world pirate game Tempest [official site] lets you step your leather boots onto solid ground for the first time. Treasure Lands DLC adds a new ship and invites you onto shore to assault forts, dig up treasure, defend villages and explore ancient cities.

If you missed it, Tempest is an adventure across the high seas, with quests to complete, crew members to manage and plenty of boom-y cannon combat. Brendan thought its large, fantasy world full of sea monsters had promise but that its missions were generally about as fun as scrubbing the poop deck. Still, one of his main criticisms was the lack of gameplay variety, which this DLC certainly addresses.

[h1]Part I[/h1]

Battle locations are back. While loading, the space is being analyzed and if it appears to be very empty, a location emerges there. As a result, there will be 136 locations on the first map, filling the emptiness. By the way, there is loot at the locations so there is an opportunity to get some bonuses.

And I’m also experimenting with a view from a captain’s place, it turns out to be a great fun:

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/ea42ad83230b99e9a6be06ae5187a9e0.gif[/img]

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/228141106fcbe9b7b175af14b91a47f0.gif[/img]

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/7fd721037f1094ea2f1df27bbf845538.gif[/img]

[b]Other improvements[/b]:
[list]

[*]Rating system for the fractions has been changed.
[*]The penalty for shooting at the ship that is located perpendicularly to the player has been re-duced.
[/list]


[h1]Part II[/h1]

I worked on a board graphics a little, adding animation for a rotation of a steering wheel right on the ship:

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/aff5c61f0a71dabf52a37bd8f6cb3f69.gif[/img]

I discovered that furrowing the seas and taking part into battles with the first person view is very exciting...

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/43eb5448b7602aa9d4b3a2ae4d8e5be8.jpg[/img]


Also, I changed mechanics of the crew’s impact on ship parameters. Now there is an opportunity to take the sea even without a crew, but in this case reloading the guns takes 100 seconds, aiming takes 30-40 seconds, and a player without a crew loses 80% of ship speed on a global map.

And now the Black Jack for factions will be available with the starter pack. There is a new slot in the decor interface where you can set the Black Jack for factions. Now a fort can treat us as an ally only if we have the same factional flag as the fort. It is very beneficial to have an allied fort because the player can come to the fort and deal under its protection with enemies shadowing the ship early on.

[b]Other improvements[/b]:
[list]
[*]The equipment system has been changed. Now it is not necessary to equip sails, skin or guns to take the sea.
[/list]



[h1]Good news : The Open World Beta Test is coming really soon. Stay tuned and good hunting! [/h1]

notes.title: Tempest - Дневник разработчика #3
notes.content:
[quote=Joruba]
Эй, на корабле!

С декабря, c самого первого дня нашего участия в раннем доступе, мы получили огромное количество отзывов и пожеланий от игроков. 
Самый популярный запрос - сделать открытый мир. Это непростая задача, но Tempest получил настолько теплый прием в сообществе Steam, что мы решили попробовать.
Это дневник разработчика будет обновляться на регулярной основе. Вести его будет [i]Avreliy.dev[/i] - ведущий разработчик игры. Этот проект остается делом его жизни уже два года, и он предельно честен касательно того, что он сможет реализовать в игре, а что нет.

Это будет очень интересно!

Пожелания, комментарии и здоровая критика только приветствуются.

[/quote]

[img]http://imageshack.com/a/img922/4006/hMAKC6.jpg[/img] 

После перехода на открытый мир надо править дизайн игры. Для начала поменял механику событий в игре. Вот так теперь выглядят встречи в море:

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/32d1178190f4bc27c163cdfe73f6284a.gif[/img]

Больше никаких постоянных остановок из-за назойливого всплывающего окна. Каждое новое событие замедляет скорость передвижения корабля. Если же три события активны, значит, игрока окружили, и он едва движется.


[b]Другие изменения:[/b]

[list] 

[*]корабль больше не ремонтируется после боя к полному значению, он ремонтируется постепенно со временем до 60%.
[*]возобновление энергии артефактов изменено (при старом времени это было 5 единиц в сутки, теперь 5 в час).
[*]скорость корабля на карте теперь рассчитывается так же как и в открытом море. Влияет эффективность, перегруз, направление ветра.
[*]перегруз теперь работает иначе, чем сильнее загружен корабль, тем больше замедляется корабль. Максимальное замедление -70%
[*]Каждое новое событие замедляет скорость передвижения корабля. Если же три события активны, значит, игрока фактически окружили, и он едва движется.
[/list]

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/24acf6b3e87fa0478cf8bf6778c4e58a.png[/img]

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/478a9af3fe3ee8dec92f077bf6f5e0e7.png[/img]

According to my calculations, it would take one hour to sail from one corner of the map to another. And with battles and repairs it can turn into a real expedition.

[list]
[*]Auto battle disabled for now. It`s not working properly in the open world.

[*]Map time sustained 14 times to match to open world sailing.
[*]Exact time in GUI.

[b]Change log:[/b]
[list]
[*]Created an automatic islandS generation.
[/list]

[h1]Day 4[/h1]
Woke up at 4 a.m. with a thought of how to connect battles, open world and multiplayer. Fell asleep, woke up again at the morning, wrote everything down in “to do” list, continued to work of the visuals.
Added cities and forts, changed the fog of war. Now it looks very cool and very transparent) And it can overlay the settlement icons.

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/f5014046c80ffeda651875b582c2a90c.png[/img]

Had to finalize locations so they would look presentable.

Pinned the HP icon the way it would be seen from any angle. And it`s 1 a.m. again.

[b]Change log:[/b]
[list]
[*]Finished locations in the open world.
[*]Had a good sleep finally.  
[/list]

[h1]Day 5[/h1]

Made ships HP visible on the map. 
City`s and fraction`s names are visible on top of the screen.

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/d6b49b370f5bc7faad523b1dd64062fa.jpg[/img]

The ship on the map now visualized as a ship (unexpected, huh?)

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/130dff37abecfa00b659cb99c5e05e1a.png[/img]

At last a gif of exiting open world into a map.

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/a66ae06843701e4104784911b22c9bf0.gif[/img]

[b]Change log:[/b]
[list]
[*]Made a cool model of a ship on the map
[*]Made number of changes in GUI
[/list]

notes.content:
[quote=Joruba]
Ahoy!

Since the very first day of Early Access in December we received tons of feedback about what people want to see in [i]Tempest[/i].
Open world is the most wanted feature. It's not a small task, but the game got such warm welcome from Steam community that we decided to give it a shot. This devblog will be updated on a constant basis by [i]Avreliy.dev[/i]. He is a lead developer of [i]Tempest[/i], this project has been his lifework for the last two years and he is extremely honest about what is possible and what is not.

This should be interesting.

Comments, feedback and suggestions are most welcome.

[/quote]

[img]http://imageshack.com/a/img923/7335/EurLrn.jpg[/img]

[h1]Day 1[/h1]

Hello everyone! 

I made an additional branch in the project to try building the open world, most likely it will become our core branch eventually.
My vision is to preserve the global map and also to allow a free roam from town to town on the tactical map.

[b] Сhange log:[/b] 

Interface changed in order to merge both battle and ship UIs

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/b4bc2c61ffdb0e5e201b8463b47e7611.png[/img]

Global map's UI changed too, it has less buttons now

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/821fae715d80606d51f80e08f2dc293c.jpg[/img]

As soon as hostiles approach, UI switches to the battle mode

[img]https://i.gyazo.com/05604982ddbcf5d5cc45a3812a1c776e.png[/img]

[b] Changes and problems of the open world feature:[/b] 

[list]
[*]Dynamic change of Day/Night is needed for sailing on the tactical map
[*]Towns' locations must be redone, since they were originally designed for a single side view
[*]Terms like 'VICTORY' and 'FLEEING' are gone since it's a free roam, you can always ignore and/or avoid AI
[*]Faction reputation won't work as it does now, same can be said about encounters
[*]Multiplayer must evolve too - it is to be linked to player's exact coordinates in the world
[*]Story content will stay mostly intact, though it will be adapted to new mechanics
[*]Navigating in the sea will possibly depend on the sun and a compass, but a player will have to find and equip it in the first place
[*]Global and tactical maps must be scaled to each other, which is tricky
[/list]

That'll be all for the day 1, how do you like it?

Good hunting out there.

notes.title: Tempest - Update #3 (New Map, New Ships and New Quests)
notes.content:
Ahoy! Third major update is here and it offers tons of fresh new content incl. a second map, more ships and quests. Definitely not the last update, we still got a long sail ahead!

[b]New game is required![/b]

[img]http://imageshack.com/a/img922/1750/YDul8N.jpg[/img]
[i]Tempest is two months old and look – we're growing![/i]

[h1]What's new:[/h1]
[list]
[*] Second map is available
[*] Ten quests for Pirates, two of them are available from the start, positive relations with the faction must be gained for other eight.
[*] Faction traits added for every settlement:
[i]Pirates[/i] - 70% repair and 200 rust cannon balls free of charge
[i]Seekers[/i] - energy refillment
[i]Black Flame[/i] - crew training
[i]Kingdom[/i] - banking services, deposits up to 15k coins
[i]Dominion[/i] - 30 fire shells for free
[i]Protectorate[/i] - free heal
[i]Returners[/i] - damage your crew in exchange for 5% chance to gain an artifact
[i]Order[/i] - a pay in gold for a chance to gain extra rating
[i]Trade Coalition[/i]- better prices.

[img]http://s12.postimg.org/4hyio978t/image.jpg[/img]
[i]New world awaits...[/i]

[*] The Flying Dutchman is invincible again, she also has three Kraken artifacts to prevent player's escape.
[*] Speed has different impact on ship's maneuvering.
[*] Quest button is now active in Port Menu.
[*] Officer skill of looting is less profitable.
[*] Small ships now have less armor effect.
[*] Aiming buttons layout for battle interface is different.
[*] Energy regens only by 5 points in midnight.
[*] Forts now have longer reload time, they also don't shoot all at once.
[*] Boarding damage formula reworked - a boarding party with low HP will now do better.


[img]http://s12.postimg.org/oa0onjist/image.jpg[/img]
[i]So much to do...[/i]

[*] Positive rating bonus for battles is lesser now.
[*] Speed on the global map is reduced.
[*] Repairs are now 100% more costly.
[*] 3 events for the allies of Pirate faction and 2 for their enemies.
[*] Death penalty is now 30% instead of 20% since there is a bank to stash gold now.
[*] Sea monsters now have better visuals.
[*] Some ports sell ship decorations.
[*] Forts don't attack a player anymore.
[*] Pricing on medicines is adjusted.
[*] Boarding: musket volley has a reload indicator.
[*] Battle Menu shows an approximate power of each side.
[*] Loot Button works differently - it takes 70% of loot from defeated enemies, hidden stashes must be found and collected manually.

[img]http://s12.postimg.org/gg0325azx/image.jpg[/img]
[i]Beauty - isn't she?[/i]

[*] List of goods is reworked.
[*] Base ship stats are lowered (aim, zone of fire).
[*] Initial rate of fire is lowered by one point.
[*] Ships cost more.
[*] Carronades are not as useful as used to be.
[*] High-aim mode gives a narrower zone of fire.
[*] A number of available quests is now shown above port icons on the global map.
[*] Escaping from a battle is forbidden for the first 30 seconds.
[*] Overall tweaking and bugfixes
[/list]

Good hunting!

- Now you can also repair your ships in villages (although not up to 100%)
- Entry points to a battle have been improved (further from enemies now)
- Game progress reset button has been added (available in setup menu)
- More screen resolutions support 
-Default language bug has been fixed
-Lots of minor tweaking and bug fixes

Multiplayer explained: from now on, in any battle, there`s a chance to play against or with other player. A real player would have a nickname right next to his ships marker.


Have fun and happy hunting!:boarding:
